title: [Chapitre] IV. Analysis situs (première mouture) : notes manuscrites (10/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (from p.35): Grothendieck is axiomatizing a 'contrée' M. M is a set of 'cells' with two relations. One is a closure/incidence relation ≪ (with < used for the strict face relation). The other picks out 'figures', which are families of pairwise compatible elements, apparently closed under taking faces. 'Lieux' (points) are the ≪-minimal elements, and L is the set of lieux. The 'ombre' (shadow) of X is L_X = {x ∈ L : x ≪ X}, and its 'open shadow' is L°_X = L_X \ ∪_{Y<X} L_Y. The shadow of a figure F is L_F = ∪_{X∈F} L_X. Two axioms are in force. Cond 3' says each M_{≤X} is finite (elementary figures are finite). Cond 4 says (a) L°_X ≠ ∅, and (b) compatible distinct X, Y have disjoint open shadows.

Scholie (this page). Let F be a figure.
(a) The map X ↦ X̃ := L_X, from F to P(L), is injective. Its image F̃ is an 'admissible' family of subsets of L, meaning two things. (α) The intersection of two members is the union of the members it contains. (β) For each X̃, put ∂X̃ := ∪{Ỹ ∈ F̃ : Ỹ ⊊ X̃} and X̃° := X̃ \ ∂X̃; then X̃° ≠ ∅. A marginal definition sets ∂X as the figure {Y ∈ M : Y < X}, 'le bord'. X̃° is called the open shadow of X on L, and ∂X̃ the shadow of the (closed) boundary.
(b) The map X ↦ X̃° is injective, and the open shadows form a partition of L_F indexed by F.
(c) The order on F is the one induced by inclusion of shadows. For X, Y in F the following are equivalent: (i) X ≤ Y; (ii) X̃ ⊆ Ỹ; (iii) X̃° ⊆ Ỹ; (iv) X̃° ∩ Ỹ ≠ ∅.

In modern terms, a figure is realized combinatorially as a finite 'regular cell complex on a point set'. Closed cells are unions of open cells, open cells partition the support, and the face order is recovered from the frontier condition (iv)⇒(i). This is the combinatorial skeleton of a stratified space satisfying the frontier condition, i.e. the face poset with its Alexandrov-type 'shadow' realization.

Purpose: this is part of the 1986 'Analysis situs' attempt (tame topology, cf. Esquisse §5–6). The goal is a purely combinatorial notion of space (contrée), with points (lieux), cells and figures. In it, topological notions (open part, boundary, closure, subfigures as closed subsets, p.37) are derived from the incidence data alone.
errors: The transcription indexes the boundary union by Ỹ ≠ X̃. With that index ∂X̃ would include cells not inside X̃. The image shows (and the mathematics requires) Ỹ ⊊ X̃, i.e. Ỹ ∈ F̃, Ỹ ⊂ X̃, Ỹ ≠ X̃.

The proofs are left implicit but go through from Cond 3' and Cond 4. The partition L_X = ⊔_{Z≤X} L°_Z follows by descending induction, which needs finiteness / well-foundedness of M_{≤X}. Disjointness follows from Cond 4b, using that the elements of a figure are pairwise compatible. (iv)⇒(i): if x ∈ X̃° ∩ Ỹ, then x ∈ Z̃° for some Z ≤ Y, and disjointness forces Z = X. Injectivity of both maps and (α) follow.

One implicit assumption needs checking: ∂X is defined in the margin with Y ∈ M, Y < X, while ∂X̃ in (β) is defined within F̃. These agree only if figures are closed downward under <. This is presumably one of the Fig axioms but is not stated on this page.

ideas.what: Recovering a finite cell complex from its point-shadows: closed cells are unions of open cells, open cells partition the support, and the face order is inclusion of closures
ideas.modern_name: Face poset of a regular CW / polyhedral complex; stratification by open cells; Alexandrov topology on a finite poset
ideas.usually_credited_to: Alexandrov (1937) for finite poset spaces; Björner (1984) for face posets of regular CW complexes; classical combinatorial topology
ideas.where_published: Only programmatic hints in Esquisse d'un programme (1984), §5 on tame topology; the contrée axiomatics are unpublished

ideas.modern_name: Frontier condition for stratifications (a stratum meeting the closure of another lies in it)
ideas.where_published: unsure; only general remarks on stratified structures in the Esquisse

ideas.what: Points ('lieux') as ≪-minimal elements, with 'ombre' and 'ombre ouverte' attached to each cell; a purely incidence-theoretic definition of the topological notions of open part and boundary
ideas.modern_name: Specialization order / poset-stratified sets; abstract cell complexes (Tucker, Kovalevsky)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Tucker (1933), Kovalevsky (1989) for abstract cell complexes

missed.claim: This page documents part of Grothendieck's unpublished axiomatics of 'contrées': points as ≪-minimal cells, shadows, figures. In it, cell complexes are characterized intrinsically by the incidence data together with a point set. It is a combinatorial foundation intended for tame topology. The page's own result is routine, but the overall framework is absent from the literature.
missed.quote: les images forment une partition de l'ombre L_F de la figure F, indexée par F
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It is of historical interest for how Grothendieck intended to found 'topologie modérée' combinatorially. It could be compared with o-minimal cell decompositions and with poset-stratified spaces / exit-path categories (Lurie, Ayala–Francis–Tanaka). It is not a new theorem.

deep.surprise_reason: The scholie itself is a standard fact about regular cell complexes and the frontier condition, derived from his axioms. It is interesting only as a witness of the unpublished 'contrée' framework of 1986.
transcription_corrections: Boundary union index: 'Ỹ ∈ F̃, Ỹ ⊊ X̃' (not 'Ỹ ≠ X̃').
'ensemble de parties "divisible"' is probably '"admissible"', consistent with 'rel. d'admissibilité' on p.37.
'l'ensemble ouvert de X̃ sur L' is likely 'l'ombre ouverte de X sur L', and the boundary phrase reads roughly 'l'ombre du bord' (corrected from 'ensemble fermé').
The margin is likely 'Déf: ∂X = {Y ∈ M | Y < X}, la figure ..., i.e. ... de X, le bord'.
The inner items α), β) under Scholie a) are transcribed as a), b).
